title: Verification harness, tests and repository checks
objective: Make verification honest and small: `verify` that provides its fixtures and never calls a skip a pass, no test that cannot fail, documentation that matches the code, a repository check that keeps each concept on one path, one rule for load-independent tests, one sRGB reference, one launch path and one distribution for every timing tool, `raw-editor` as a scenario, scenarios written as plans plus pixel claims, a structured architecture document, `editor-acceptance` limited to what `cargo test` cannot prove, and fewer test binaries.
context_summary: The harness consolidation landed its core: one smoke table and plan library that derive scripts and frame counts, universal per-frame checks, a replay and a mutation proof, one serde evidence script, `luxforge-testkit`, an independent `luxforge-reference` and one percentile in xtask. It stopped at the edges: timing tools and `raw-editor` still launch and watch editors their own way, every scenario hand-writes its own evidence records, state checks and photo finders across roughly 13,600 lines for 18 scenarios, `verify` has two honesty defects, and some tests cannot fail. Test code is about 46% of the tree; each group plan deletes its own duplicates, and this plan owns the shared rules and the harness-wide pieces. The owner's decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions.md`; the programme's constraints are in `docs/design/post-consolidation.md`; verification practice is in `docs/engineering/development.md`.

tasks.description: Make fixture generation idempotent and derive `verify`'s fixture requirement from one table, so a checkout whose `fixtures/generated/` predates the range fixture still passes `verify --tier rendered` instead of failing at setup.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. A skip in fixture generation stops the tier the owner runs at integration points before its RAW and rendered components ever run.

`xtask/src/fixtures.rs`'s `generate` writes five files (24 MP, 60 MP, hue wheel, presence, range) but refuses outright when its output directory already exists; `xtask/src/verify.rs`'s own `GENERATED` list names only four of them, omitting `range.jpg`, which the `mask-range` scenario opens. `verify` schedules generation only when one of its four is missing, so a checkout whose fixtures directory predates the range fixture never regenerates it and `mask-range` fails; whenever the directory exists but lacks any one of the four, `verify`'s setup component fails outright and the whole tier stops there.
A new agent worktree hides this because it starts with no fixtures directory at all; a long-lived checkout, such as the owner's, does not.
Constraint: `generate-fixtures` must stay safe to run against an existing directory: write only what is missing, and refuse only a hash mismatch against the manifest, never an already-correct file.

tasks.description: Report a `verify` tier with any skipped or unrun component as incomplete, with a distinct non-zero exit naming what was skipped, and run the authentic RAW tests and `hardening` where a manifest and the full tier make them possible.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. `verify` is the honesty check the owner runs before trusting a milestone claim, and today it can report success while proving less than it looks like.

`Status::failure` in `xtask/src/verify.rs` counts only `failed` and `timed_out`, and a unit test pins `skipped` and `not_run` as equivalent to a pass. So the headline, `summary.json`'s status and the process exit code all read as success when `verify --tier full` runs with no `--manifest`: the RAW components are silently absent from the plan rather than recorded as skipped, and the only trace is one table row.

The authentic RAW native and JSON tests, in `luxforge-raw` and `luxforge-app`, are all `#[ignore]`d behind an owner-supplied RAW directory and sit in no tier at all, even when a manifest is given; `hardening`'s process-failure and never-frontmost checks are in no tier either.
Owner decision: `verify` reports a tier with a skipped or unrun component as incomplete, with a distinct non-zero exit naming what was skipped.
Constraint: `summary.json`'s shape may change freely (current shapes only; nothing outside this tool reads it).

tasks.description: Delete or rewrite the tests that cannot fail because they compare a value with a copy of itself or wait on a status no job reaches, and add the stroke-deletion test that actually proves a removed stroke stops affecting coverage.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. A test that cannot fail is counted as coverage; there are tautologies as well as a chapter step that fabricates its own outcome instead of asserting one.

In the core: two mask tests build both sides of their comparison from the same stroke list, so `mask.delete-stroke` could do nothing and both would still pass; five more compare an entry point with the cancellable function it is defined to call, or a value with its own clone, and one asserts `refine_radius(100.0) == refine_radius(100.0)`. The mask overlay module's parallel-split test runs below the one-megapixel threshold that selects the parallel path, so it compares the serial loop with itself and never reaches the branch it names.

In xtask: `basic_acceptance.rs` waits in a loop while a job's status equals `"pending"`, a status the current job vocabulary (queued, running, ready, failed, cancelled, superseded) does not have, so the loop never actually waits and the step passes only because an earlier step already cached the answer. `mask_acceptance.rs`'s changed-original step turns a refusal it expected but did not get into a fabricated `("reported", …)` result instead of asserting the refusal code, and records `null` when its fixture is absent.

Constraint: the overlay fix must inject a low threshold for the test rather than lowering the production default, and the new stroke test must fail when a mask implementation is changed to fold every stored stroke rather than only the kept ones. Where a test is deleted outright rather than rewritten, the commit names the kept test that proves the same property.

tasks.description: Generalize `check-repository`'s three layering rules into a table of (token, allowed paths, reason) entries covering what already holds today, so a later task that finishes a concept can add its own one-path rule to the same mechanism.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. Every task in this programme that finishes a concept is expected to add the repository rule that keeps it single; this task builds the table those rules go into.

`xtask/src/repository.rs`'s `BOUNDARIES` constant enforces exactly three rules today: the desktop's view model may not reach Iced or `app::`; its view may not reach the core or call the owner directly; the widget crate may not reach the core at all. Nothing mechanical stops a second commit path, worker thread, owner-call helper or limit constant from returning once one is removed; every such leftover is findable with a grep, so a check can refuse it.

Proposal: generalize `BOUNDARIES` into a table of (token, allowed path prefixes, reason), checked over `crates/` and `xtask/`, with each rule choosing whether it covers test code. Seed it with rules that already hold today: thread spawning confined to the declared worker locations, no `Handle::from_rgba` anywhere in the app, and no bare `lightwell` identifier anywhere in source.
Document in `docs/engineering/development.md` that a task finishing a concept adds its own rule to this table rather than inventing a bespoke check.

tasks.description: State one rule for tests that must not depend on host load, no shared state, ordering from gates not sleeps, a deadline that only bounds a hang, and give every crate a core-free gate and wait helper in testkit, fixing the load-dependent tests found.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. Four flakes have already been fixed one at a time; this states the rule that stops the next one and gives every crate the tool the fixes need.

The core's unit tests share one static render context across a whole test binary whose tests run in parallel: two mutexes serialize the tests that read shared budgets, dozens of call sites reset a shared estimate store, and several tests assert exact in-use or peak figures that any other concurrently running render can move. This is the same shape as a recently recorded flake in the RAW crate, where an admitted-permit count came in short because something outside a shared lock still held a slot.

Elsewhere, ordering is assumed from elapsed time rather than a gate: a desktop evidence test scripts a wait and asserts the very next tick sees nothing, which a scheduling delay between the two calls can violate; a preview-queue test asserts a second held job is pending without first waiting for the first job to reach its own gate; a spatial-render test raises its cancellation from a thread that merely sleeps 20 ms and panics if the render finished first; a capability journey test uses a proof endpoint's ten-second delay as if it were a gate that opens on its own schedule. Speed is also asserted in the default, non-timing suite: a process-counters test spins for 200 ms and requires 150 ms of measured CPU time, three capability tests bound their own promptness at two seconds, and a shared test server sleeps 50 ms and asserts the result lands in under a second.

The core already has a `RenderGate`/`HeldModule` pair for exactly this purpose, but it is `pub(crate)` and test-only, so the desktop keeps its own separate copy of the same idea rather than sharing it.
Constraint: the shared gate and wait helper must not depend on `luxforge-core`, so the core's own unit tests can use them too; each crate adds a small adapter rather than a second implementation.

The check-repository rule table this plan builds elsewhere gains an entry forbidding a second private test-ordering gate or wait helper outside `luxforge-testkit`, naming the shared `Gate`/`wait_until` as the one place to extend.

tasks.description: Give tests one sRGB reference module in `luxforge-reference`, with named decode, encode and quantize variants, and replace the private sRGB transcriptions scattered across test code with it.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. A disagreeing oracle is worse than none: this is the same duplication an earlier consolidation task removed from production colour math, still present in the tests that check it.

Test code carries roughly twenty private copies of sRGB decode, encode and quantize across the reference crate's own studies and the core's unit and integration tests, under a handful of shared names that actually mean three different functions: encoding clamped to `[0, 1]`, encoding clamped only below zero, and encoding left unclamped, with rounding written as both `floor(x + 0.5)` and `round()`. The reference crate itself exports its decode function under three aliased names.

Proposal: one `luxforge_reference::srgb` module with named variants (`decode`, `decode_encoded`, `encode_clamped`, `encode_nonnegative`, `encode_extended`, `quantize`, `code`), with the old aliases deleted and every study and test calling the new module.

Constraint: no committed number may move. The reference crate's own reload tests, which recompute each frozen corpus and fail on drift, must pass unchanged, and every production-against-reference comparison keeps its existing tolerance.
The check-repository rule table gains an entry forbidding a private sRGB transfer-function transcription outside `luxforge_reference::srgb`.

tasks.description: Split the loopback test server and other core-free helpers out of `luxforge-testkit` into a crate with no core dependency, so a core `--lib` edit builds the core once, and merge the app's three CLI test binaries and `resources_cost` into their siblings.
extra_context: Wave 5, tests. `cargo test --workspace` builds 24 test executables; 13 link `luxforge-core`, and the core itself dev-depends on `luxforge-testkit`, which depends back on the core, so the recommended edit loop of testing the core's library alone builds the core twice.

That cycle is also why the core's own tens of thousands of lines of unit tests cannot use testkit's typed helpers: a `luxforge-core` type inside testkit is a different type from the one the core's own unit tests see. The result is duplication testkit was meant to remove: several private `mutation` helpers inside the core's unit tests alone, near-identical owner test harnesses in two capability test files, and the same small SQL-seeding helper repeated in two mask test files.

The core already has three small test-support modules (`editor/test_support.rs`, `capabilities/testing.rs`, `artifacts/testing.rs`); this consolidates future owner-harness and mutation-envelope helpers there instead of adding a fourth.

Separately, three of the app's `tests/` binaries each spin up their own process for a small, non-overlapping slice of CLI behavior, and one core integration binary (`resources_cost`) is a single ignored test that could run inside another binary instead.

tasks.description: Clear the harness's remaining small defects: dead fields, a Windows-incompatible test, redundant CI jobs, hard-coded scenario lists, copied desktop formatters, an uninjectable buffer-size constant, and run-log prose in the development guide.
extra_context: Wave 5, tests. Depends on the one distribution type landing first, since one of these items, `editor-latency`'s dead `upload_ms` field, is otherwise entangled with the timing report shape that task settles.

Portability: `verify`'s pool tests spawn `/bin/sleep`, so `cargo test -p xtask` cannot pass on Windows, where CI only runs `cargo xtask check`; spawn the xtask test binary itself instead, as the scenario launch tests already do, or confine the sleep-based tests to Unix.

Redundant or drifted checks: the CI fixtures job re-runs the same fixture check `check`'s own test run already runs as `golden_corpus`; the CI Linux smoke step hard-codes eight scenario names instead of iterating `smoke --list`; `docs/engineering/development.md`'s CI section says CI runs `cargo xtask check` and that Linux runs every smoke scenario, when the workflow actually runs `verify --tier quick` and the same eight named scenarios.

Dead and copied code: `editor-latency` carries an `upload_ms`/`gpu_upload` field the editor never emits, backed by a test that fabricates the value it checks; the harness re-implements the desktop's own byte, percentage and elapsed-time formatters instead of importing them, and the two copies already disagree on how a non-finite value prints; the core's artifact LRU accounting test fills real 64 MiB buffers because its size constant cannot be injected, when a parameterized bound would let it test with kilobytes.

Prose: `docs/engineering/development.md` carries a dated scenario-workload quote and a per-run measurement log that duplicate figures this plan's other tasks keep current elsewhere, plus roughly 180 lines restating each scenario's own plan, which duplicates what each scenario's module doc already provides to `smoke --list`.
Constraint: each item in this task is independent; where a fix is not worth its own change, explain why in the commit rather than leaving it silently undone.
